dedupe_keys.name: israel public transport licensed daily bus trips by line 2017 onward and rail planned versus operated trips

description: Two operational datasets from Israel's Ministry of Transport describe how much public transport service is licensed and delivered. Contents: the bus system licensing database gives the number of daily licensed trips per bus line, with one CSV per year from 2017 to 2026 and a data structure document; the rail planned versus operated dataset lists, by year, month, train number, origin and destination station, the licensed trips, trips licensed but not operated, trips operated without a licence and the percentage performed for Israel Railways. Producer: the ministry's public transport division, from its licensing and monitoring systems. Coverage: all licensed bus lines and national rail services in Israel. Format and access: CSV files with PDF data dictionaries on data.gov.il, also reachable through the CKAN datastore API; the bus file is refreshed daily. Free under the portal's open terms. Caveats: the rail file notes that no new data are currently expected, so it may stay frozen, and the bus file counts scheduled licensed trips, not observed runs; Hebrew field names. Simulation uses: service supply inputs for transit models, calibration of frequencies, and measuring service reliability and disruption effects on the rail network. Related records: the ministry's planning GIS layers (data-israel-ministry-of-transport-planning-gis-layers) give stations, frequencies and tunnels.
